tool.name: vt_reputation
tool.description:
Look up an IoC (hash / IP / domain / URL) in VirusTotal and surface the multi-engine reputation verdict. First 🔴 critical item from the §10 expert-pentester gap audit. Different signal from the single-source feeds in `domain_reputation` (#63) — VirusTotal's value is the *consensus* across 70+ AV/EDR vendors.
Auto-detects IoC type from input shape:
| IoC type | Detected by | VT endpoint | |---|---|---| | md5 / sha1 / sha256 / sha512 | hex string of 32/40/64/128 chars | `/api/v3/files/` | | ip | parses as `ipaddress.ip_address` (private/loopback/link-local rejected) | `/api/v3/ip_addresses/` | | domain | apex/subdomain regex | `/api/v3/domains/` | | url | starts with `http://` / `https://` | `/api/v3/urls/` |
Severity tuning (based on VT's `last_analysis_stats`): - **High** (CWE-453, malicious_target) — `malicious >= 10` engines (high-confidence consensus across many vendors). - **Medium** (CWE-453) — `malicious + suspicious >= 3` engines. - **Low** (CWE-453) — `malicious + suspicious >= 1` engines. - *(no finding)* — clean across all vendors.
Auth: `STRIX_VT_KEY` env var (free tier available at virustotal.com — 4 req/min, 500/day). Without it, returns `success=False` with a clear error so the agent falls back to other reputation sources.
Cache: per-(ioc_type, ioc_value) JSON cache under `~/.strix/vt_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. Stale-cache served on network failure (fail-open with `error` populated). When cache is hit, findings re-emitted from cached stats. Disable with `STRIX_VT_NO_CACHE=1`.
VT 404 response (no data on this IoC) is treated as success with empty stats and `no_data=True`, NOT as failure.
Each finding carries severity-tailored `description_plain` + `recommended_action`: - HIGH → "treat as compromised, trigger IR, rebuild from known-clean, rotate credentials, request re-scan". - MEDIUM → "investigate, cross-reference flagging vendors with your tooling, escalate to hosting provider if shared infrastructure". - LOW → "informational; cross-reference with other reputation sources before acting".
`verification_status=needs_review` since reputation verdicts can carry stale data.
MITRE technique: T1596 (Search Open Technical Databases).
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to the VT request; `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URL is api.virustotal.com, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: ioc
parameter.description: Indicator value. Auto-detected as one of: MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 hash (hex string), IPv4/IPv6 address (private/loopback/link-local rejected), domain (apex/subdomain), URL (must start with `http://` or `https://`). URL targets are URL-safe-base64-encoded for VT's URL endpoint internally.

returns.description:
{success, ioc, ioc_type, vt_url, queried_at, from_cache, stats: {malicious, suspicious, harmless, undetected, timeout}, severity, reputation, flagging_engines: [name, ...], attributes: {last_analysis_date, country_code, as_owner, categories, ...}, findings_emitted, error?, no_data?}.
The agent should: 1. Cross-reference VT verdicts with `domain_reputation` (#63) single-source feeds for full picture. 2. Use `flagging_engines[]` to surface specific vendor detection names to the user — those are useful for SIEM rule mapping. 3. Note `attributes.country_code` / `attributes.as_owner` for IPs to enrich attribution context. 4. Treat `no_data=True` as "VT hasn't seen this IoC" (not a clean verdict — VT just hasn't been asked about it before).
